name: Simeon
description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: On the third day, when they were sore, two of the sons, Simeon and Levi, took each man his sword, came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males; they took Dinah out, spoiled the city, and carried away the substance and the households.

Two men do not take a city alone. The sword of Simeon was given of God to take vengeance of the strangers that defiled the maid; they were moved with the zeal of the Most High, and He was behind the judgment.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

points: He turned himself about from them and wept, for he heard everything they said; then he returned, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.

note.label: Genesis 42: Joseph's Brethren Bow Down in Egypt

points: Every man's bundle of money was in his sack, and they were afraid; and Jacob their father said, me have ye bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away.

note.label: Genesis 42: Joseph's Brethren Bow Down in Egypt

points: Thy two sons Ephraim and Manasseh, as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine. Jacob took Joseph's sons as his own, so the blessings that came upon Jacob's sons came upon Ephraim and Manasseh also; they became children of Israel, partakers of the same promises as the rest of the sons of Jacob.

note.label: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel

points: Simeon and Levi are brethren and their children would be together in the last days, which is seen in Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

note.label: Haiti: the Rise After the Ruin

points: Some of you have doubt the Haitian is not really Levi. Simeon and Levi are brethren. Now, you notice he say Simeon and Levi are brothers, but the whole 12 is brothers. Why he specifically mention Simeon and Levi? The so-called Haitian and Dominican: map shown, that's the same island. They're divided, but they're in the same island. In other words, at the end, those two going to be together in the same island. One part called Haiti, one part called Dominican Republic.

Be not thou united: guess what, they're not united. One time this used to be one island; now they're divided. One part Simeon, one part Levi. As a matter of fact, they hate each other. Dominicans cannot stand Haitians; Haitians cannot stand Dominicans.

note.label: Know Your Enemy: God's Foes & Ours

points: Simeon and Levi are brethren: in the last days the so-called Haitians and the so-called Dominicans are living on the same island of Hispaniola. Instruments of cruelty are in their habitations: that's going into the witchcraft, the voodoo and black magic. Unto their assembly, mine honour, be not thou united: that's why the Haitians and the Dominicans hate each other and are not united; that's why you see them snatching people off the street and deporting them.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

points: Simeon is the so-called Dominican and Levi the so-called Haitian today. Simeon and Levi are brethren: all the tribes of Israel are brethren, but these two in particular were to dwell together, and they share the same island, Hispaniola.

Instruments of cruelty are in their habitations: the witchcraft practiced on that island, such as the voodoo of Haiti. O my soul, come not thou into their secret: because of those practices the Most High does not unite them, and the two nations stay divided on the island even though Levi helped free Simeon from slavery.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

points: Tribe by tribe, by their generations, after their families, by the house of their fathers, every male from twenty years old and upward able to go forth to war was numbered: Reuben 46,500; Simeon 59,300; Gad 45,650; Judah 74,600; Issachar 54,400; Zebulun 57,400; Ephraim 40,500; Manasseh 32,200; Benjamin 35,400; Dan 62,700; Asher 41,500; Naphtali 53,400.

note.label: Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel

points: Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

points: The second lot came forth to Simeon, and their inheritance was within the inheritance of the children of Judah.

On the map the whole land Judah possessed is marked as one, and within it sits the portion where Simeon resided, down by Beer-sheba. The so-called Dominicans, of Simeon, were living within the land of the so-called African Americans, of Judah; this is our history and where we lived.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families, out of the portion of the children of Judah: for the part of the children of Judah was too much for them.
Judah had a lot of area and was being his brother's keeper: come dwell with us, Simeon, we got you; therefore the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The cities came out by lot family by family: the children of Aaron the priest, of the Kohathites, had thirteen cities out of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin; the rest of the children of Kohath had ten cities out of Ephraim, Dan, and the half tribe of Manasseh.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

points: Out of Judah and Simeon the children of Aaron received nine cities by name, and out of Benjamin four more, thirteen cities in all for the priests.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

points: Judah asks Simeon his brother to come up with him into his lot, and promises to go likewise with Simeon into his lot, so Simeon went with him.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: Judah goes with Simeon his brother, slays the Canaanites in Zephath and utterly destroys it, calling the city Hormah, and takes Gaza, Askelon, and Ekron with their coasts.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The twelve sons of Israel are set down: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: Five hundred of the sons of Simeon went to mount Seir, smote the remnant of the Amalekites that had escaped, and dwelt there, showing the Most High's blessing on them in war.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 4: The Families of Judah and Simeon

points: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon. Notice they're calling Ephraim and Manasseh strangers. So there was some that loved the Lord. That's good; very important on the street.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Asa gathers Judah, Benjamin, and the strangers out of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, who fell to him in abundance when they saw the Most High was with him. These strangers are Israelites whose hearts turned back.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 15: The Covenant to Seek the Most High

cases.name: Simeon and Levi at Shechem
cases.charge: Deceitful covenant; slaughter of a city in their anger
cases.preview: Dinah went out to see the daughters of the land without supervision, and Shechem the prince of the country took her and defiled her.
